newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Predators stalk undervalued UK trusts.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Predators stalk undervalued UK trusts.

text.p: Britain's investment trust sector faced further upheaval on Thursday amid growing concern about poor returns and deeply discounted share prices.
News that U.S. hedge fund Sierra Trading bought 10 percent of Govett Oriental Investment Trust and HSBC's bid to unseat the manager of the Saracen Value Trust was well received by investors.
Govett Oriental's share rose to a 52-week high of 188 pence and Saracen's jumped three pence to 92 -- but both remained at substantial discounts to net asset value (NAV).
The developments added to a string of recent changes in the trust sector.
Last week Fleming Far Eastern proposed to wind its activities down and return cash to shareholders.
At issue in all three cases is shareholders' desire to realise hidden value, analysts said.
Because investment trusts are closed ended they can trade at discounts to the value of the underlying assets, and do so when managers or types of funds fall out of favour.
Even with Thursday's rise, Saracen is trading at 19 percent discount to NAV and Govett Oriental is at a 12 percent discount.
In the past year Saracen shares have lost 5.1 percent versus a 2.4 percent gain in its peer group, according to Micropal.
In the same period, Govett Oriental lost 1.25 percent on its share price, versus a peer group return of 1.03 percent.
But Govett's 5-year gain of 165.8 percent places it first in its peer group.
"If Asia and small caps were booming none of this would be an issue," said John Korwin-Szymanowski, an analyst at SBC Warburg.
There is also a general oversupply of investment trusts, he added, leading even good performers to trade at a discount.
Sierra Trading purchased the position, worth about 65 million pounds, from SBC Warburg.
"With a holding of ten percent he must be meaning to try and force some change in the structure of the trust," said Simon Colson, an analyst at NatWest Securities.
Govett officials declined to comment but analysts believe that it is likely to put up a fight if pressured to liquidate the fund.
"This is an important investment trust for Govett and they are likely to defend it robustly," Colson said.
Govett Oriental, at 650 million pounds, represent a sizeable share of John Govett & Co's $5.5 billion under management.
HSBC Investment Management has approached the board of Saracen and said it had the support of shareholders representing 49.3 percent of Saracen's issued share capital.
The directors of Saracen are advising shareholders not to take any action.
HSBC said in a statement it was proposing to waive its management fee for the first two years of any contract and to reduce the notice period from two years to one year at the end of three years.
After two years, HSBC also will reduce the management fee to O.75 percent from the current one percent of total assets less liabilities.
Saracen defended its performance in a statement and said that it has retained Charterhouse Tilney Securities to "explore means of maximising value for shareholders".
